acceptance_checks: A task blocked by another task's active lock produces a named blocked-on-lock result carrying the owning task id and the overlapping locks.
The stop is distinguishable in loop output from a guardian stop and from a blocked-evidence stop.
A conflict over several locks with one owner produces one message, not one per lock.
A goal whose every task is lock-blocked reports that fact rather than appearing idle.
non_goals: Making the loop wait or retry on a conflict
scope: scripts/shiki_loop.py _unblock_ready_tasks does `ok, blockers, _ = try_acquire_locks(...); if not ok: continue` — no ledger entry, no stop, no reason. A serialized queue therefore presents as a deadlock, which is exactly how the PR #179 stall read. Emit a blocked-on-lock stop naming the owning task and the overlapping locks, and deduplicate active_lock_conflicts to one message per owner rather than one per (held lock x owner) pair.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Name the lock-conflict stop instead of skipping silently
